
AISA API Platform  |  April 2026

# Executive Summary

The AISA API Platform currently uses DynamoDB as its primary database. As the platform has evolved to include admin dashboards, analytics, audit logging, feedback management, and a knowledge base management, the data access patterns now require capabilities that DynamoDB cannot provide natively — specifically aggregations, multi-dimensional filtering and analytics.

Recommendation: Adopt Aurora PostgreSQL as the primary database. It handles all current access patterns — from chat writes to complex admin dashboards — in a single managed service. The team already has existing Aurora infrastructure in place, minimizing setup effort.

# Comparison: Aurora PostgreSQL vs DynamoDB

|   |   |   |
|---|---|---|
|**Criteria**|**DynamoDB**|**Aurora PostgreSQL**|
|**Structured Data**|No enforcement — schemaless, application must validate everything|Full SQL with types, constraints, and foreign keys|
|**Semi-structured Data**|Native (schemaless)|Native (JSONB) — query, index, and aggregate into JSON|
|**Unstructured Text Search**|Needs OpenSearch as additional service|Built-in (tsvector/tsquery) — no extra service needed|
|**SQL Features  <br>(JOINs, GROUP BY, search, analytics)**|None|All — full PostgreSQL SQL support|
|**Read / Write Speed**|Fast for simple key-value lookups. Slow for aggregations, analytics, and search (requires full table scans). Text search not possible without additional service.|Fast for all query types — key-value lookups, aggregations, analytics, and full-text search are all native and optimized.|
|**Scaling Model**|Serverless|Provisioned (managed by AWS)|
|**Existing Infrastructure**|Serverless|Team already has existing Aurora infrastructure — cluster, networking, security, monitoring, backups, and operational expertise all in place|

# Decision

**Aurora PostgreSQL** — supports all data types (structured, semi-structured, unstructured), full SQL capabilities (JOINs, aggregations, full-text search, analytics), fast performance across all query patterns, and leverages the team's existing Aurora infrastructure.

## Key Reasons

·       Supports structured data with full SQL types, constraints, and foreign keys

·       Supports semi-structured data natively via JSONB columns

·       Built-in unstructured text search (tsvector) — no additional service required

·       Full SQL support: JOINs, GROUP BY, aggregations, window functions, CTEs

·       Fast read/write for all query types — key-value lookups, aggregations, analytics, and search are all native and optimized

·       Team already has existing Aurora PostgreSQL infrastructure — cluster, networking, security, monitoring, backups, and operational expertise in place

·       Single database replaces multiple services (DynamoDB + OpenSearch + Streams)

·       Standard SQL — portable queries, no vendor lock-in on query language
